resume: Finding a leisure center for Wednesdays and school holidays, preparing the file (up-to-date vaccinations, family quotient) and learning about leisure-time aid from the Caf de La Réunion.
aQuoiCaSert: Non-residential leisure centers (ALSH, accueils de loisirs sans hébergement, often called centres de loisirs) take children from the time they start school up to adolescence, including children with disabilities. Depending on the town, they open on Wednesdays, before or after school, at lunchtime and during school holidays. Each organizer, town hall or association, sets its own prices, often based on household income and support from the Caf (Caisse d'allocations familiales, the family benefits office). The Caf de La Réunion also offers leisure-time aid (aides au temps libre) for children's stays and family holidays.
quiEstConcerne: Parents of school-age children looking for care on Wednesdays or during the holidays.
Low-income families receiving Caf benefits, for the leisure-time and holiday aid of the Caf de La Réunion.
aSavoir: Places are limited: find out several weeks before the holidays or the start of the school year. You usually register at the town hall (mairie) or directly with the center.

Mandatory vaccinations are required for admission to group settings, including leisure centers and holiday camps. The list depends on the child's year of birth. There is no mandatory vaccine specific to Réunion.
If vaccinations are not up to date, the child can be admitted provisionally: you then have 3 months to catch up. The health record book (carnet de santé) filled in by the doctor serves as proof.
Leisure-time aid comes under each Caf's own social action program: amounts and conditions vary from one département to another and sometimes from one year to the next.

Separated parents: each parent can register the child for their own holiday weeks. Tell the center who is authorized to pick up the child and, if needed, provide the decision setting the child's residence.
